count_semantics_notes: CDPH and CDC ArboNET distinguish between 'neuroinvasive disease' (encephalitis, meningitis, acute flaccid paralysis) and 'non-neuroinvasive disease' (West Nile fever); map neuroinvasive to cases_confirmed where lab-confirmed.

Confirmed cases require laboratory confirmation (IgM in CSF, PRNT, or PCR); probable cases typically have IgM in serum with epidemiologic linkage — ensure case classification is preserved in extraction.
CDPH weekly reports are cumulative year-to-date; to derive August-specific counts, subtract the July 31 cumulative total from the August 31 cumulative total where possible.
ArboNET data may lag real-time reporting by 1–2 weeks; August 2024 data may not be finalized until late September or October 2024.
Dead bird, sentinel chicken, and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — exclude from cases_confirmed/probable fields; they may be noted as contextual surveillance indicators only.
County-level reports may use 'suspected' or 'under investigation' categories that do not map directly to confirmed/probable — flag as cases_suspected or cases_unspecified accordingly.
Some county reports aggregate multi-week data; note the reporting period explicitly in evidence_quote to avoid double-counting across records.
disambiguation_risks: WNV surveillance reports often combine human and animal/vector data — isolate human case counts only.
'Cases' in some county reports may refer to mosquito pool positives or dead bird detections, not human infections — read context carefully.
Neuroinvasive disease case counts are a subset of total WNV human cases — do not add neuroinvasive + non-neuroinvasive if the source already reports a combined total.
CDPH reports are cumulative year-to-date; do not treat a single weekly report's total as the count for that week alone.
ArboNET data for 2024 may be preliminary and subject to revision — note data status (preliminary vs. final) in source metadata.
'Probable' case definitions vary between CDPH and CDC/ArboNET — document the case definition used by the source.
Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, and San Bernardino counties historically report the highest WNV burden in California — absence of data from these counties should trigger a data gap flag.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about West Nile Virus Disease.

count_semantics_notes: CDPH and CDC ArboNET distinguish between 'neuroinvasive disease' (encephalitis, meningitis, acute flaccid paralysis) and 'non-neuroinvasive disease' (West Nile fever); map neuroinvasive to cases_confirmed where lab-confirmed.

Confirmed cases require laboratory confirmation (IgM in CSF, PRNT, or PCR); probable cases typically have IgM in serum with epidemiologic linkage — ensure case classification is preserved in extraction.
CDPH weekly reports are cumulative year-to-date; to derive August-specific counts, subtract the July 31 cumulative total from the August 31 cumulative total where possible.
ArboNET data may lag real-time reporting by 1–2 weeks; August 2024 data may not be finalized until late September or October 2024.
Dead bird, sentinel chicken, and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — exclude from cases_confirmed/probable fields; they may be noted as contextual surveillance indicators only.
County-level reports may use 'suspected' or 'under investigation' categories that do not map directly to confirmed/probable — flag as cases_suspected or cases_unspecified accordingly.
Some county reports aggregate multi-week data; note the reporting period explicitly in evidence_quote to avoid double-counting across records.
disambiguation_risks: WNV surveillance reports often combine human and animal/vector data — isolate human case counts only.
'Cases' in some county reports may refer to mosquito pool positives or dead bird detections, not human infections — read context carefully.
Neuroinvasive disease case counts are a subset of total WNV human cases — do not add neuroinvasive + non-neuroinvasive if the source already reports a combined total.
CDPH reports are cumulative year-to-date; do not treat a single weekly report's total as the count for that week alone.
ArboNET data for 2024 may be preliminary and subject to revision — note data status (preliminary vs. final) in source metadata.
'Probable' case definitions vary between CDPH and CDC/ArboNET — document the case definition used by the source.
Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, and San Bernardino counties historically report the highest WNV burden in California — absence of data from these counties should trigger a data gap flag.

count_semantics_notes: CDPH and CDC ArboNET distinguish between 'neuroinvasive disease' (encephalitis, meningitis, acute flaccid paralysis) and 'non-neuroinvasive disease' (West Nile fever); map neuroinvasive to cases_confirmed where lab-confirmed.

Confirmed cases require laboratory confirmation (IgM in CSF, PRNT, or PCR); probable cases typically have IgM in serum with epidemiologic linkage — ensure case classification is preserved in extraction.
CDPH weekly reports are cumulative year-to-date; to derive August-specific counts, subtract the July 31 cumulative total from the August 31 cumulative total where possible.
ArboNET data may lag real-time reporting by 1–2 weeks; August 2024 data may not be finalized until late September or October 2024.
Dead bird, sentinel chicken, and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — exclude from cases_confirmed/probable fields; they may be noted as contextual surveillance indicators only.
County-level reports may use 'suspected' or 'under investigation' categories that do not map directly to confirmed/probable — flag as cases_suspected or cases_unspecified accordingly.
Some county reports aggregate multi-week data; note the reporting period explicitly in evidence_quote to avoid double-counting across records.
disambiguation_risks: WNV surveillance reports often combine human and animal/vector data — isolate human case counts only.
'Cases' in some county reports may refer to mosquito pool positives or dead bird detections, not human infections — read context carefully.
Neuroinvasive disease case counts are a subset of total WNV human cases — do not add neuroinvasive + non-neuroinvasive if the source already reports a combined total.
CDPH reports are cumulative year-to-date; do not treat a single weekly report's total as the count for that week alone.
ArboNET data for 2024 may be preliminary and subject to revision — note data status (preliminary vs. final) in source metadata.
'Probable' case definitions vary between CDPH and CDC/ArboNET — document the case definition used by the source.
Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, and San Bernardino counties historically report the highest WNV burden in California — absence of data from these counties should trigger a data gap flag.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about West Nile Virus Disease.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

count_semantics_notes: CDPH and CDC ArboNET distinguish between 'neuroinvasive disease' (encephalitis, meningitis, acute flaccid paralysis) and 'non-neuroinvasive disease' (West Nile fever); map neuroinvasive to cases_confirmed where lab-confirmed.

Confirmed cases require laboratory confirmation (IgM in CSF, PRNT, or PCR); probable cases typically have IgM in serum with epidemiologic linkage — ensure case classification is preserved in extraction.
CDPH weekly reports are cumulative year-to-date; to derive August-specific counts, subtract the July 31 cumulative total from the August 31 cumulative total where possible.
ArboNET data may lag real-time reporting by 1–2 weeks; August 2024 data may not be finalized until late September or October 2024.
Dead bird, sentinel chicken, and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — exclude from cases_confirmed/probable fields; they may be noted as contextual surveillance indicators only.
County-level reports may use 'suspected' or 'under investigation' categories that do not map directly to confirmed/probable — flag as cases_suspected or cases_unspecified accordingly.
Some county reports aggregate multi-week data; note the reporting period explicitly in evidence_quote to avoid double-counting across records.
disambiguation_risks: WNV surveillance reports often combine human and animal/vector data — isolate human case counts only.
'Cases' in some county reports may refer to mosquito pool positives or dead bird detections, not human infections — read context carefully.
Neuroinvasive disease case counts are a subset of total WNV human cases — do not add neuroinvasive + non-neuroinvasive if the source already reports a combined total.
CDPH reports are cumulative year-to-date; do not treat a single weekly report's total as the count for that week alone.
ArboNET data for 2024 may be preliminary and subject to revision — note data status (preliminary vs. final) in source metadata.
'Probable' case definitions vary between CDPH and CDC/ArboNET — document the case definition used by the source.
Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, and San Bernardino counties historically report the highest WNV burden in California — absence of data from these counties should trigger a data gap flag.

source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV case counts that can serve as an independent validation source against CDPH figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC Wonder or other structured federal databases with California WNV case or death records for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured federal databases provide independently compiled counts that can be compared against primary state sources for validation without leakage risk.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH or CDC case definition documents for West Nile virus neuroinvasive disease and non-neuroinvasive disease to support correct classification of extracted counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definitions determine whether counts are confirmed, probable, or suspected and whether neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive classifications apply, which affects field mapping.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or surveillance reports describing WNV epidemiology in California in 2024 for contextual interpretation of count semantics and reporting lags.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret whether reported counts are cumulative-to-date, newly reported in the period, or reflect reporting lag adjustments.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news reports from August 2024 citing official California WNV case or death figures to triangulate collection records and identify additional official source URLs.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports often cite official sources and can serve as pointers to primary data pages or press releases not easily discoverable via direct search.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that mix human and animal/veterinary WNV data, report only mosquito pool positives or sentinel chicken seroconversions, or present cumulative annual counts without August-specific breakdowns for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources mixing excluded terms (animal WNV, mosquito pool positive, sentinel chicken) or lacking date-specific human case counts must be reviewed before extraction to avoid contaminating the collection record.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDPH publishes the authoritative California WNV human case surveillance statistics, including weekly updates, annual summaries, and county-level breakdowns with neuroinvasive/non-neuroinvasive classification. Primary collection source for all target fields.

County health departments in high-burden California counties (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, San Bernardino, Riverside, Stanislaus, Tulare) publish local WNV situation updates and press releases that may contain August 2024 case and death data at finer geographic resolution than state reports.

CalVBDS is California's integrated vectorborne disease surveillance platform and may provide structured, downloadable human WNV case data with county, date, and classification fields directly usable for extraction.
CDC ArboNET and CDC DVBD publish national WNV surveillance summaries with state-level breakdowns. These serve as independent validation sources against CDPH-reported figures for California 2024.
CDC ArboNET open data, CDC Wonder, or California open data portals may provide structured, machine-readable WNV case records for California 2024 suitable for validation cross-checks.
Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies or surveillance reports on WNV in California provide case definitions, count semantics, and historical context for interpreting 2024 surveillance data.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., Los Angeles Times, Sacramento Bee, CalMatters) and public health alert services may report on WNV outbreaks in California during August 2024, citing official figures and linking to primary sources.

validation_source_categories: County-level health department press releases or situation reports
count_semantics_notes: CDPH and CDC ArboNET distinguish between 'neuroinvasive disease' (encephalitis, meningitis, acute flaccid paralysis) and 'non-neuroinvasive disease' (West Nile fever); map neuroinvasive to cases_confirmed where lab-confirmed.

Confirmed cases require laboratory confirmation (IgM in CSF, PRNT, or PCR); probable cases typically have IgM in serum with epidemiologic linkage — ensure case classification is preserved in extraction.
CDPH weekly reports are cumulative year-to-date; to derive August-specific counts, subtract the July 31 cumulative total from the August 31 cumulative total where possible.
ArboNET data may lag real-time reporting by 1–2 weeks; August 2024 data may not be finalized until late September or October 2024.
Dead bird, sentinel chicken, and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — exclude from cases_confirmed/probable fields; they may be noted as contextual surveillance indicators only.
County-level reports may use 'suspected' or 'under investigation' categories that do not map directly to confirmed/probable — flag as cases_suspected or cases_unspecified accordingly.
Some county reports aggregate multi-week data; note the reporting period explicitly in evidence_quote to avoid double-counting across records.
disambiguation_risks: WNV surveillance reports often combine human and animal/vector data — isolate human case counts only.
'Cases' in some county reports may refer to mosquito pool positives or dead bird detections, not human infections — read context carefully.
Neuroinvasive disease case counts are a subset of total WNV human cases — do not add neuroinvasive + non-neuroinvasive if the source already reports a combined total.
CDPH reports are cumulative year-to-date; do not treat a single weekly report's total as the count for that week alone.
ArboNET data for 2024 may be preliminary and subject to revision — note data status (preliminary vs. final) in source metadata.
'Probable' case definitions vary between CDPH and CDC/ArboNET — document the case definition used by the source.
Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, and San Bernardino counties historically report the highest WNV burden in California — absence of data from these counties should trigger a data gap flag.

DATA COMPLETENESS: WNV case reporting has a known lag; August 2024 case counts may be incomplete in reports published before October 2024 — note data completeness status.
GEOGRAPHIC SCOPE: California has 58 counties; prioritize high-burden counties (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, San Bernardino, Riverside, Stanislaus) but do not exclude others.

count_semantics_notes: CDPH and CDC ArboNET distinguish between 'neuroinvasive disease' (encephalitis, meningitis, acute flaccid paralysis) and 'non-neuroinvasive disease' (West Nile fever); map neuroinvasive to cases_confirmed where lab-confirmed.

Confirmed cases require laboratory confirmation (IgM in CSF, PRNT, or PCR); probable cases typically have IgM in serum with epidemiologic linkage — ensure case classification is preserved in extraction.
CDPH weekly reports are cumulative year-to-date; to derive August-specific counts, subtract the July 31 cumulative total from the August 31 cumulative total where possible.
ArboNET data may lag real-time reporting by 1–2 weeks; August 2024 data may not be finalized until late September or October 2024.
Dead bird, sentinel chicken, and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — exclude from cases_confirmed/probable fields; they may be noted as contextual surveillance indicators only.
County-level reports may use 'suspected' or 'under investigation' categories that do not map directly to confirmed/probable — flag as cases_suspected or cases_unspecified accordingly.
Some county reports aggregate multi-week data; note the reporting period explicitly in evidence_quote to avoid double-counting across records.
disambiguation_risks: WNV surveillance reports often combine human and animal/vector data — isolate human case counts only.
'Cases' in some county reports may refer to mosquito pool positives or dead bird detections, not human infections — read context carefully.
Neuroinvasive disease case counts are a subset of total WNV human cases — do not add neuroinvasive + non-neuroinvasive if the source already reports a combined total.
CDPH reports are cumulative year-to-date; do not treat a single weekly report's total as the count for that week alone.
ArboNET data for 2024 may be preliminary and subject to revision — note data status (preliminary vs. final) in source metadata.
'Probable' case definitions vary between CDPH and CDC/ArboNET — document the case definition used by the source.
Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, and San Bernardino counties historically report the highest WNV burden in California — absence of data from these counties should trigger a data gap flag.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH (California Department of Public Health) West Nile virus surveillance pages, weekly or monthly situation reports, and statistical tables reporting human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in California during August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDPH is the primary state-level authority for WNV human case surveillance in California and publishes weekly/annual WNV statistics disaggregated by county and disease classification (neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive).

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify county-level public health department reports (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, San Bernardino, Riverside, Stanislaus, Tulare) for WNV human cases and deaths reported in August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: High-burden California counties often publish their own WNV situation updates, press releases, and dashboards that may contain locally-specific case counts and dates not yet aggregated at the state level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California Vectorborne Disease Surveillance System (CalVBDS) data or dashboards reporting human WNV cases for the August 2024 period.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CalVBDS is the state's integrated vectorborne disease surveillance platform and may provide structured, downloadable case data with date, county, and case classification fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify vector control district reports (Sacramento-Yolo MVCD, Greater Los Angeles County Vector Control District, Coachella Valley MVCD) that include human case counts for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Vector control districts in California publish weekly or biweekly WNV activity reports that sometimes include human case tallies alongside mosquito surveillance data.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET or CDC DVBD West Nile virus surveillance summaries for California 2024 to cross-validate state-reported case and death counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV case counts that can serve as an independent validation source against CDPH figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC Wonder or other structured federal databases with California WNV case or death records for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured federal databases provide independently compiled counts that can be compared against primary state sources for validation without leakage risk.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH or CDC case definition documents for West Nile virus neuroinvasive disease and non-neuroinvasive disease to support correct classification of extracted counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definitions determine whether counts are confirmed, probable, or suspected and whether neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive classifications apply, which affects field mapping.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or surveillance reports describing WNV epidemiology in California in 2024 for contextual interpretation of count semantics and reporting lags.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret whether reported counts are cumulative-to-date, newly reported in the period, or reflect reporting lag adjustments.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news reports from August 2024 citing official California WNV case or death figures to triangulate collection records and identify additional official source URLs.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports often cite official sources and can serve as pointers to primary data pages or press releases not easily discoverable via direct search.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that mix human and animal/veterinary WNV data, report only mosquito pool positives or sentinel chicken seroconversions, or present cumulative annual counts without August-specific breakdowns for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources mixing excluded terms (animal WNV, mosquito pool positive, sentinel chicken) or lacking date-specific human case counts must be reviewed before extraction to avoid contaminating the collection record.

count_semantics_notes: CDPH and CDC ArboNET distinguish between 'neuroinvasive disease' (encephalitis, meningitis, acute flaccid paralysis) and 'non-neuroinvasive disease' (West Nile fever); map neuroinvasive to cases_confirmed where lab-confirmed.

Confirmed cases require laboratory confirmation (IgM in CSF, PRNT, or PCR); probable cases typically have IgM in serum with epidemiologic linkage — ensure case classification is preserved in extraction.
CDPH weekly reports are cumulative year-to-date; to derive August-specific counts, subtract the July 31 cumulative total from the August 31 cumulative total where possible.
ArboNET data may lag real-time reporting by 1–2 weeks; August 2024 data may not be finalized until late September or October 2024.
Dead bird, sentinel chicken, and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — exclude from cases_confirmed/probable fields; they may be noted as contextual surveillance indicators only.
County-level reports may use 'suspected' or 'under investigation' categories that do not map directly to confirmed/probable — flag as cases_suspected or cases_unspecified accordingly.
Some county reports aggregate multi-week data; note the reporting period explicitly in evidence_quote to avoid double-counting across records.
disambiguation_risks: WNV surveillance reports often combine human and animal/vector data — isolate human case counts only.
'Cases' in some county reports may refer to mosquito pool positives or dead bird detections, not human infections — read context carefully.
Neuroinvasive disease case counts are a subset of total WNV human cases — do not add neuroinvasive + non-neuroinvasive if the source already reports a combined total.
CDPH reports are cumulative year-to-date; do not treat a single weekly report's total as the count for that week alone.
ArboNET data for 2024 may be preliminary and subject to revision — note data status (preliminary vs. final) in source metadata.
'Probable' case definitions vary between CDPH and CDC/ArboNET — document the case definition used by the source.
Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, and San Bernardino counties historically report the highest WNV burden in California — absence of data from these counties should trigger a data gap flag.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH (California Department of Public Health) West Nile virus surveillance pages, weekly or monthly situation reports, and statistical tables reporting human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in California during August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDPH is the primary state-level authority for WNV human case surveillance in California and publishes weekly/annual WNV statistics disaggregated by county and disease classification (neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive).

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify county-level public health department reports (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, San Bernardino, Riverside, Stanislaus, Tulare) for WNV human cases and deaths reported in August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: High-burden California counties often publish their own WNV situation updates, press releases, and dashboards that may contain locally-specific case counts and dates not yet aggregated at the state level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California Vectorborne Disease Surveillance System (CalVBDS) data or dashboards reporting human WNV cases for the August 2024 period.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CalVBDS is the state's integrated vectorborne disease surveillance platform and may provide structured, downloadable case data with date, county, and case classification fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify vector control district reports (Sacramento-Yolo MVCD, Greater Los Angeles County Vector Control District, Coachella Valley MVCD) that include human case counts for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Vector control districts in California publish weekly or biweekly WNV activity reports that sometimes include human case tallies alongside mosquito surveillance data.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET or CDC DVBD West Nile virus surveillance summaries for California 2024 to cross-validate state-reported case and death counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV case counts that can serve as an independent validation source against CDPH figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC Wonder or other structured federal databases with California WNV case or death records for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured federal databases provide independently compiled counts that can be compared against primary state sources for validation without leakage risk.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH or CDC case definition documents for West Nile virus neuroinvasive disease and non-neuroinvasive disease to support correct classification of extracted counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definitions determine whether counts are confirmed, probable, or suspected and whether neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive classifications apply, which affects field mapping.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or surveillance reports describing WNV epidemiology in California in 2024 for contextual interpretation of count semantics and reporting lags.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret whether reported counts are cumulative-to-date, newly reported in the period, or reflect reporting lag adjustments.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news reports from August 2024 citing official California WNV case or death figures to triangulate collection records and identify additional official source URLs.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports often cite official sources and can serve as pointers to primary data pages or press releases not easily discoverable via direct search.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that mix human and animal/veterinary WNV data, report only mosquito pool positives or sentinel chicken seroconversions, or present cumulative annual counts without August-specific breakdowns for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources mixing excluded terms (animal WNV, mosquito pool positive, sentinel chicken) or lacking date-specific human case counts must be reviewed before extraction to avoid contaminating the collection record.

CalVBDS is California's integrated vectorborne disease surveillance platform and may provide structured, downloadable human WNV case data with county, date, and classification fields directly usable for extraction.
CDC ArboNET and CDC DVBD publish national WNV surveillance summaries with state-level breakdowns. These serve as independent validation sources against CDPH-reported figures for California 2024.
CDC ArboNET open data, CDC Wonder, or California open data portals may provide structured, machine-readable WNV case records for California 2024 suitable for validation cross-checks.
Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies or surveillance reports on WNV in California provide case definitions, count semantics, and historical context for interpreting 2024 surveillance data.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., Los Angeles Times, Sacramento Bee, CalMatters) and public health alert services may report on WNV outbreaks in California during August 2024, citing official figures and linking to primary sources.

source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV case counts that can serve as an independent validation source against CDPH figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC Wonder or other structured federal databases with California WNV case or death records for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured federal databases provide independently compiled counts that can be compared against primary state sources for validation without leakage risk.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH or CDC case definition documents for West Nile virus neuroinvasive disease and non-neuroinvasive disease to support correct classification of extracted counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definitions determine whether counts are confirmed, probable, or suspected and whether neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive classifications apply, which affects field mapping.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or surveillance reports describing WNV epidemiology in California in 2024 for contextual interpretation of count semantics and reporting lags.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret whether reported counts are cumulative-to-date, newly reported in the period, or reflect reporting lag adjustments.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news reports from August 2024 citing official California WNV case or death figures to triangulate collection records and identify additional official source URLs.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports often cite official sources and can serve as pointers to primary data pages or press releases not easily discoverable via direct search.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that mix human and animal/veterinary WNV data, report only mosquito pool positives or sentinel chicken seroconversions, or present cumulative annual counts without August-specific breakdowns for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources mixing excluded terms (animal WNV, mosquito pool positive, sentinel chicken) or lacking date-specific human case counts must be reviewed before extraction to avoid contaminating the collection record.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDPH publishes the authoritative California WNV human case surveillance statistics, including weekly updates, annual summaries, and county-level breakdowns with neuroinvasive/non-neuroinvasive classification. Primary collection source for all target fields.

County health departments in high-burden California counties (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, San Bernardino, Riverside, Stanislaus, Tulare) publish local WNV situation updates and press releases that may contain August 2024 case and death data at finer geographic resolution than state reports.

CalVBDS is California's integrated vectorborne disease surveillance platform and may provide structured, downloadable human WNV case data with county, date, and classification fields directly usable for extraction.
CDC ArboNET and CDC DVBD publish national WNV surveillance summaries with state-level breakdowns. These serve as independent validation sources against CDPH-reported figures for California 2024.
CDC ArboNET open data, CDC Wonder, or California open data portals may provide structured, machine-readable WNV case records for California 2024 suitable for validation cross-checks.
Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies or surveillance reports on WNV in California provide case definitions, count semantics, and historical context for interpreting 2024 surveillance data.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., Los Angeles Times, Sacramento Bee, CalMatters) and public health alert services may report on WNV outbreaks in California during August 2024, citing official figures and linking to primary sources.

official_source_terms: California Department of Public Health West Nile virus
California Mosquito-Borne Virus Surveillance and Response Plan
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
likely_reporting_agencies: County Departments of Public Health (e.g., Los Angeles County DPH, Sacramento County DPH, Kern County DPH, Fresno County DPH, San Bernardino County DPH)
Vector control districts (e.g., Sacramento-Yolo Mosquito and Vector Control District, Greater Los Angeles County Vector Control District)
validation_source_categories: County-level health department press releases or situation reports
count_semantics_notes: CDPH and CDC ArboNET distinguish between 'neuroinvasive disease' (encephalitis, meningitis, acute flaccid paralysis) and 'non-neuroinvasive disease' (West Nile fever); map neuroinvasive to cases_confirmed where lab-confirmed.

Confirmed cases require laboratory confirmation (IgM in CSF, PRNT, or PCR); probable cases typically have IgM in serum with epidemiologic linkage — ensure case classification is preserved in extraction.
CDPH weekly reports are cumulative year-to-date; to derive August-specific counts, subtract the July 31 cumulative total from the August 31 cumulative total where possible.
ArboNET data may lag real-time reporting by 1–2 weeks; August 2024 data may not be finalized until late September or October 2024.
Dead bird, sentinel chicken, and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — exclude from cases_confirmed/probable fields; they may be noted as contextual surveillance indicators only.
County-level reports may use 'suspected' or 'under investigation' categories that do not map directly to confirmed/probable — flag as cases_suspected or cases_unspecified accordingly.
Some county reports aggregate multi-week data; note the reporting period explicitly in evidence_quote to avoid double-counting across records.
disambiguation_risks: WNV surveillance reports often combine human and animal/vector data — isolate human case counts only.
'Cases' in some county reports may refer to mosquito pool positives or dead bird detections, not human infections — read context carefully.
Neuroinvasive disease case counts are a subset of total WNV human cases — do not add neuroinvasive + non-neuroinvasive if the source already reports a combined total.
CDPH reports are cumulative year-to-date; do not treat a single weekly report's total as the count for that week alone.
ArboNET data for 2024 may be preliminary and subject to revision — note data status (preliminary vs. final) in source metadata.
'Probable' case definitions vary between CDPH and CDC/ArboNET — document the case definition used by the source.
Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, and San Bernardino counties historically report the highest WNV burden in California — absence of data from these counties should trigger a data gap flag.

iterative_search_queries.query: CDC West Nile virus 2024 California cases deaths ArboNET statistics

This provides cross-validation against CDPH figures and may include data through August 2024.

iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov domain; federal public health authority; ArboNET surveillance system

iterative_search_queries.query: West Nile virus California county August 2024 cases deaths public health department report
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: Targets county-level public health department reports for California counties with historically high WNV burden (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, Riverside, San Bernardino). County health departments often publish their own WNV updates with locality-level detail not captured in state summaries, enabling population of the 'locality' field. The broader query without rigid quoting increases recall across multiple county agency sites.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: County public health department WNV press release, advisory, or surveillance update citing case counts for August 2024
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: County .gov or .ca.gov domain; official county health officer or epidemiologist attribution

iterative_search_queries.query: West Nile virus California August 2024 cases deaths outbreak news
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: News media reports published in August 2024 frequently cite official CDPH or county health department figures and can provide dated evidence quotes, locality detail, and links to primary official sources. This query uses natural language without rigid quoting to maximize recall across news outlets covering California WNV activity during the target window.

iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: Publication date within August 2024; cites named official source (CDPH, county health officer); includes specific numeric case counts

iterative_search_queries.query: westnile.ca.gov Arbobulletin 2024 August weekly report human cases deaths site:westnile.ca.gov

The CDPH WNV bulletin numbering system runs approximately weekly; August 2024 corresponds to bulletins roughly #30–#35 of the 2024 season. A site-restricted query with 'August' and '2024' should surface the specific bulletin PDFs with week-ending dates in August 2024, enabling confirmation of the time window and extraction of case counts, deaths, and county breakdowns.

iterative_search_queries.query: CDC West Nile virus 2024 historical data cases deaths by state California neuroinvasive

The lacounty.gov result appeared in iteration 1 but its content was not confirmed for August 2024 dates or numeric data.

iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: lacounty.gov or saccounty.gov domain; county health officer or epidemiologist attribution; publication date in August 2024

count_semantics_notes: CDPH and CDC ArboNET distinguish between 'neuroinvasive disease' (encephalitis, meningitis, acute flaccid paralysis) and 'non-neuroinvasive disease' (West Nile fever); map neuroinvasive to cases_confirmed where lab-confirmed.

Confirmed cases require laboratory confirmation (IgM in CSF, PRNT, or PCR); probable cases typically have IgM in serum with epidemiologic linkage — ensure case classification is preserved in extraction.
CDPH weekly reports are cumulative year-to-date; to derive August-specific counts, subtract the July 31 cumulative total from the August 31 cumulative total where possible.
ArboNET data may lag real-time reporting by 1–2 weeks; August 2024 data may not be finalized until late September or October 2024.
Dead bird, sentinel chicken, and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — exclude from cases_confirmed/probable fields; they may be noted as contextual surveillance indicators only.
County-level reports may use 'suspected' or 'under investigation' categories that do not map directly to confirmed/probable — flag as cases_suspected or cases_unspecified accordingly.
Some county reports aggregate multi-week data; note the reporting period explicitly in evidence_quote to avoid double-counting across records.
disambiguation_risks: WNV surveillance reports often combine human and animal/vector data — isolate human case counts only.
'Cases' in some county reports may refer to mosquito pool positives or dead bird detections, not human infections — read context carefully.
Neuroinvasive disease case counts are a subset of total WNV human cases — do not add neuroinvasive + non-neuroinvasive if the source already reports a combined total.
CDPH reports are cumulative year-to-date; do not treat a single weekly report's total as the count for that week alone.
ArboNET data for 2024 may be preliminary and subject to revision — note data status (preliminary vs. final) in source metadata.
'Probable' case definitions vary between CDPH and CDC/ArboNET — document the case definition used by the source.
Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, and San Bernardino counties historically report the highest WNV burden in California — absence of data from these counties should trigger a data gap flag.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH (California Department of Public Health) West Nile virus surveillance pages, weekly or monthly situation reports, and statistical tables reporting human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in California during August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDPH is the primary state-level authority for WNV human case surveillance in California and publishes weekly/annual WNV statistics disaggregated by county and disease classification (neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive).

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify county-level public health department reports (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, San Bernardino, Riverside, Stanislaus, Tulare) for WNV human cases and deaths reported in August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: High-burden California counties often publish their own WNV situation updates, press releases, and dashboards that may contain locally-specific case counts and dates not yet aggregated at the state level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California Vectorborne Disease Surveillance System (CalVBDS) data or dashboards reporting human WNV cases for the August 2024 period.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CalVBDS is the state's integrated vectorborne disease surveillance platform and may provide structured, downloadable case data with date, county, and case classification fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify vector control district reports (Sacramento-Yolo MVCD, Greater Los Angeles County Vector Control District, Coachella Valley MVCD) that include human case counts for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Vector control districts in California publish weekly or biweekly WNV activity reports that sometimes include human case tallies alongside mosquito surveillance data.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET or CDC DVBD West Nile virus surveillance summaries for California 2024 to cross-validate state-reported case and death counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV case counts that can serve as an independent validation source against CDPH figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC Wonder or other structured federal databases with California WNV case or death records for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured federal databases provide independently compiled counts that can be compared against primary state sources for validation without leakage risk.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH or CDC case definition documents for West Nile virus neuroinvasive disease and non-neuroinvasive disease to support correct classification of extracted counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definitions determine whether counts are confirmed, probable, or suspected and whether neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive classifications apply, which affects field mapping.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or surveillance reports describing WNV epidemiology in California in 2024 for contextual interpretation of count semantics and reporting lags.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret whether reported counts are cumulative-to-date, newly reported in the period, or reflect reporting lag adjustments.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news reports from August 2024 citing official California WNV case or death figures to triangulate collection records and identify additional official source URLs.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports often cite official sources and can serve as pointers to primary data pages or press releases not easily discoverable via direct search.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that mix human and animal/veterinary WNV data, report only mosquito pool positives or sentinel chicken seroconversions, or present cumulative annual counts without August-specific breakdowns for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources mixing excluded terms (animal WNV, mosquito pool positive, sentinel chicken) or lacking date-specific human case counts must be reviewed before extraction to avoid contaminating the collection record.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDPH publishes the authoritative California WNV human case surveillance statistics, including weekly updates, annual summaries, and county-level breakdowns with neuroinvasive/non-neuroinvasive classification. Primary collection source for all target fields.

County health departments in high-burden California counties (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, San Bernardino, Riverside, Stanislaus, Tulare) publish local WNV situation updates and press releases that may contain August 2024 case and death data at finer geographic resolution than state reports.

CalVBDS is California's integrated vectorborne disease surveillance platform and may provide structured, downloadable human WNV case data with county, date, and classification fields directly usable for extraction.
CDC ArboNET and CDC DVBD publish national WNV surveillance summaries with state-level breakdowns. These serve as independent validation sources against CDPH-reported figures for California 2024.
CDC ArboNET open data, CDC Wonder, or California open data portals may provide structured, machine-readable WNV case records for California 2024 suitable for validation cross-checks.
Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies or surveillance reports on WNV in California provide case definitions, count semantics, and historical context for interpreting 2024 surveillance data.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., Los Angeles Times, Sacramento Bee, CalMatters) and public health alert services may report on WNV outbreaks in California during August 2024, citing official figures and linking to primary sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH (California Department of Public Health) West Nile virus surveillance pages, weekly or monthly situation reports, and statistical tables reporting human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in California during August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDPH is the primary state-level authority for WNV human case surveillance in California and publishes weekly/annual WNV statistics disaggregated by county and disease classification (neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive).

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify county-level public health department reports (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, San Bernardino, Riverside, Stanislaus, Tulare) for WNV human cases and deaths reported in August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: High-burden California counties often publish their own WNV situation updates, press releases, and dashboards that may contain locally-specific case counts and dates not yet aggregated at the state level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California Vectorborne Disease Surveillance System (CalVBDS) data or dashboards reporting human WNV cases for the August 2024 period.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CalVBDS is the state's integrated vectorborne disease surveillance platform and may provide structured, downloadable case data with date, county, and case classification fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify vector control district reports (Sacramento-Yolo MVCD, Greater Los Angeles County Vector Control District, Coachella Valley MVCD) that include human case counts for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Vector control districts in California publish weekly or biweekly WNV activity reports that sometimes include human case tallies alongside mosquito surveillance data.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET or CDC DVBD West Nile virus surveillance summaries for California 2024 to cross-validate state-reported case and death counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV case counts that can serve as an independent validation source against CDPH figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC Wonder or other structured federal databases with California WNV case or death records for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured federal databases provide independently compiled counts that can be compared against primary state sources for validation without leakage risk.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH or CDC case definition documents for West Nile virus neuroinvasive disease and non-neuroinvasive disease to support correct classification of extracted counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definitions determine whether counts are confirmed, probable, or suspected and whether neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive classifications apply, which affects field mapping.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or surveillance reports describing WNV epidemiology in California in 2024 for contextual interpretation of count semantics and reporting lags.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret whether reported counts are cumulative-to-date, newly reported in the period, or reflect reporting lag adjustments.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news reports from August 2024 citing official California WNV case or death figures to triangulate collection records and identify additional official source URLs.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports often cite official sources and can serve as pointers to primary data pages or press releases not easily discoverable via direct search.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that mix human and animal/veterinary WNV data, report only mosquito pool positives or sentinel chicken seroconversions, or present cumulative annual counts without August-specific breakdowns for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources mixing excluded terms (animal WNV, mosquito pool positive, sentinel chicken) or lacking date-specific human case counts must be reviewed before extraction to avoid contaminating the collection record.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDPH publishes the authoritative California WNV human case surveillance statistics, including weekly updates, annual summaries, and county-level breakdowns with neuroinvasive/non-neuroinvasive classification. Primary collection source for all target fields.

County health departments in high-burden California counties (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, San Bernardino, Riverside, Stanislaus, Tulare) publish local WNV situation updates and press releases that may contain August 2024 case and death data at finer geographic resolution than state reports.

CalVBDS is California's integrated vectorborne disease surveillance platform and may provide structured, downloadable human WNV case data with county, date, and classification fields directly usable for extraction.
CDC ArboNET and CDC DVBD publish national WNV surveillance summaries with state-level breakdowns. These serve as independent validation sources against CDPH-reported figures for California 2024.
CDC ArboNET open data, CDC Wonder, or California open data portals may provide structured, machine-readable WNV case records for California 2024 suitable for validation cross-checks.
Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies or surveillance reports on WNV in California provide case definitions, count semantics, and historical context for interpreting 2024 surveillance data.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., Los Angeles Times, Sacramento Bee, CalMatters) and public health alert services may report on WNV outbreaks in California during August 2024, citing official figures and linking to primary sources.

count_semantics_notes: CDPH and CDC ArboNET distinguish between 'neuroinvasive disease' (encephalitis, meningitis, acute flaccid paralysis) and 'non-neuroinvasive disease' (West Nile fever); map neuroinvasive to cases_confirmed where lab-confirmed.

Confirmed cases require laboratory confirmation (IgM in CSF, PRNT, or PCR); probable cases typically have IgM in serum with epidemiologic linkage — ensure case classification is preserved in extraction.
CDPH weekly reports are cumulative year-to-date; to derive August-specific counts, subtract the July 31 cumulative total from the August 31 cumulative total where possible.
ArboNET data may lag real-time reporting by 1–2 weeks; August 2024 data may not be finalized until late September or October 2024.
Dead bird, sentinel chicken, and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — exclude from cases_confirmed/probable fields; they may be noted as contextual surveillance indicators only.
County-level reports may use 'suspected' or 'under investigation' categories that do not map directly to confirmed/probable — flag as cases_suspected or cases_unspecified accordingly.
Some county reports aggregate multi-week data; note the reporting period explicitly in evidence_quote to avoid double-counting across records.
disambiguation_risks: WNV surveillance reports often combine human and animal/vector data — isolate human case counts only.
'Cases' in some county reports may refer to mosquito pool positives or dead bird detections, not human infections — read context carefully.
Neuroinvasive disease case counts are a subset of total WNV human cases — do not add neuroinvasive + non-neuroinvasive if the source already reports a combined total.
CDPH reports are cumulative year-to-date; do not treat a single weekly report's total as the count for that week alone.
ArboNET data for 2024 may be preliminary and subject to revision — note data status (preliminary vs. final) in source metadata.
'Probable' case definitions vary between CDPH and CDC/ArboNET — document the case definition used by the source.
Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, and San Bernardino counties historically report the highest WNV burden in California — absence of data from these counties should trigger a data gap flag.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH (California Department of Public Health) West Nile virus surveillance pages, weekly or monthly situation reports, and statistical tables reporting human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in California during August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDPH is the primary state-level authority for WNV human case surveillance in California and publishes weekly/annual WNV statistics disaggregated by county and disease classification (neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive).

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify county-level public health department reports (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, San Bernardino, Riverside, Stanislaus, Tulare) for WNV human cases and deaths reported in August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: High-burden California counties often publish their own WNV situation updates, press releases, and dashboards that may contain locally-specific case counts and dates not yet aggregated at the state level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California Vectorborne Disease Surveillance System (CalVBDS) data or dashboards reporting human WNV cases for the August 2024 period.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CalVBDS is the state's integrated vectorborne disease surveillance platform and may provide structured, downloadable case data with date, county, and case classification fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify vector control district reports (Sacramento-Yolo MVCD, Greater Los Angeles County Vector Control District, Coachella Valley MVCD) that include human case counts for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Vector control districts in California publish weekly or biweekly WNV activity reports that sometimes include human case tallies alongside mosquito surveillance data.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET or CDC DVBD West Nile virus surveillance summaries for California 2024 to cross-validate state-reported case and death counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV case counts that can serve as an independent validation source against CDPH figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC Wonder or other structured federal databases with California WNV case or death records for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured federal databases provide independently compiled counts that can be compared against primary state sources for validation without leakage risk.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH or CDC case definition documents for West Nile virus neuroinvasive disease and non-neuroinvasive disease to support correct classification of extracted counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definitions determine whether counts are confirmed, probable, or suspected and whether neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive classifications apply, which affects field mapping.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or surveillance reports describing WNV epidemiology in California in 2024 for contextual interpretation of count semantics and reporting lags.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret whether reported counts are cumulative-to-date, newly reported in the period, or reflect reporting lag adjustments.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news reports from August 2024 citing official California WNV case or death figures to triangulate collection records and identify additional official source URLs.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports often cite official sources and can serve as pointers to primary data pages or press releases not easily discoverable via direct search.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that mix human and animal/veterinary WNV data, report only mosquito pool positives or sentinel chicken seroconversions, or present cumulative annual counts without August-specific breakdowns for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources mixing excluded terms (animal WNV, mosquito pool positive, sentinel chicken) or lacking date-specific human case counts must be reviewed before extraction to avoid contaminating the collection record.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH (California Department of Public Health) West Nile virus surveillance pages, weekly or monthly situation reports, and statistical tables reporting human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in California during August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDPH is the primary state-level authority for WNV human case surveillance in California and publishes weekly/annual WNV statistics disaggregated by county and disease classification (neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive).

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify county-level public health department reports (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, San Bernardino, Riverside, Stanislaus, Tulare) for WNV human cases and deaths reported in August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: High-burden California counties often publish their own WNV situation updates, press releases, and dashboards that may contain locally-specific case counts and dates not yet aggregated at the state level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California Vectorborne Disease Surveillance System (CalVBDS) data or dashboards reporting human WNV cases for the August 2024 period.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CalVBDS is the state's integrated vectorborne disease surveillance platform and may provide structured, downloadable case data with date, county, and case classification fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify vector control district reports (Sacramento-Yolo MVCD, Greater Los Angeles County Vector Control District, Coachella Valley MVCD) that include human case counts for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Vector control districts in California publish weekly or biweekly WNV activity reports that sometimes include human case tallies alongside mosquito surveillance data.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET or CDC DVBD West Nile virus surveillance summaries for California 2024 to cross-validate state-reported case and death counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV case counts that can serve as an independent validation source against CDPH figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC Wonder or other structured federal databases with California WNV case or death records for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured federal databases provide independently compiled counts that can be compared against primary state sources for validation without leakage risk.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH or CDC case definition documents for West Nile virus neuroinvasive disease and non-neuroinvasive disease to support correct classification of extracted counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definitions determine whether counts are confirmed, probable, or suspected and whether neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive classifications apply, which affects field mapping.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or surveillance reports describing WNV epidemiology in California in 2024 for contextual interpretation of count semantics and reporting lags.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret whether reported counts are cumulative-to-date, newly reported in the period, or reflect reporting lag adjustments.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news reports from August 2024 citing official California WNV case or death figures to triangulate collection records and identify additional official source URLs.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports often cite official sources and can serve as pointers to primary data pages or press releases not easily discoverable via direct search.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that mix human and animal/veterinary WNV data, report only mosquito pool positives or sentinel chicken seroconversions, or present cumulative annual counts without August-specific breakdowns for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources mixing excluded terms (animal WNV, mosquito pool positive, sentinel chicken) or lacking date-specific human case counts must be reviewed before extraction to avoid contaminating the collection record.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDPH publishes the authoritative California WNV human case surveillance statistics, including weekly updates, annual summaries, and county-level breakdowns with neuroinvasive/non-neuroinvasive classification. Primary collection source for all target fields.

County health departments in high-burden California counties (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, San Bernardino, Riverside, Stanislaus, Tulare) publish local WNV situation updates and press releases that may contain August 2024 case and death data at finer geographic resolution than state reports.

CalVBDS is California's integrated vectorborne disease surveillance platform and may provide structured, downloadable human WNV case data with county, date, and classification fields directly usable for extraction.
CDC ArboNET and CDC DVBD publish national WNV surveillance summaries with state-level breakdowns. These serve as independent validation sources against CDPH-reported figures for California 2024.
CDC ArboNET open data, CDC Wonder, or California open data portals may provide structured, machine-readable WNV case records for California 2024 suitable for validation cross-checks.
Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies or surveillance reports on WNV in California provide case definitions, count semantics, and historical context for interpreting 2024 surveillance data.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., Los Angeles Times, Sacramento Bee, CalMatters) and public health alert services may report on WNV outbreaks in California during August 2024, citing official figures and linking to primary sources.

count_semantics_notes: CDPH and CDC ArboNET distinguish between 'neuroinvasive disease' (encephalitis, meningitis, acute flaccid paralysis) and 'non-neuroinvasive disease' (West Nile fever); map neuroinvasive to cases_confirmed where lab-confirmed.

Confirmed cases require laboratory confirmation (IgM in CSF, PRNT, or PCR); probable cases typically have IgM in serum with epidemiologic linkage — ensure case classification is preserved in extraction.
CDPH weekly reports are cumulative year-to-date; to derive August-specific counts, subtract the July 31 cumulative total from the August 31 cumulative total where possible.
ArboNET data may lag real-time reporting by 1–2 weeks; August 2024 data may not be finalized until late September or October 2024.
Dead bird, sentinel chicken, and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — exclude from cases_confirmed/probable fields; they may be noted as contextual surveillance indicators only.
County-level reports may use 'suspected' or 'under investigation' categories that do not map directly to confirmed/probable — flag as cases_suspected or cases_unspecified accordingly.
Some county reports aggregate multi-week data; note the reporting period explicitly in evidence_quote to avoid double-counting across records.
disambiguation_risks: WNV surveillance reports often combine human and animal/vector data — isolate human case counts only.
'Cases' in some county reports may refer to mosquito pool positives or dead bird detections, not human infections — read context carefully.
Neuroinvasive disease case counts are a subset of total WNV human cases — do not add neuroinvasive + non-neuroinvasive if the source already reports a combined total.
CDPH reports are cumulative year-to-date; do not treat a single weekly report's total as the count for that week alone.
ArboNET data for 2024 may be preliminary and subject to revision — note data status (preliminary vs. final) in source metadata.
'Probable' case definitions vary between CDPH and CDC/ArboNET — document the case definition used by the source.
Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, and San Bernardino counties historically report the highest WNV burden in California — absence of data from these counties should trigger a data gap flag.

input.user_request: Collect West Nile virus cases, deaths, dates, locations, source URLs, source types, and evidence quotes for California from 2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31.

structured_task.user_request: Collect West Nile virus cases, deaths, dates, locations, source URLs, source types, and evidence quotes for California from 2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31.

collection_spec.data_focus: human West Nile virus case, outbreak, and surveillance data
collection_spec.user_request: Collect West Nile virus cases, deaths, dates, locations, source URLs, source types, and evidence quotes for California from 2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31.

official_source_terms: California Department of Public Health West Nile virus
California Mosquito-Borne Virus Surveillance and Response Plan
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
likely_reporting_agencies: County Departments of Public Health (e.g., Los Angeles County DPH, Sacramento County DPH, Kern County DPH, Fresno County DPH, San Bernardino County DPH)
Vector control districts (e.g., Sacramento-Yolo Mosquito and Vector Control District, Greater Los Angeles County Vector Control District)
validation_source_categories: County-level health department press releases or situation reports
count_semantics_notes: CDPH and CDC ArboNET distinguish between 'neuroinvasive disease' (encephalitis, meningitis, acute flaccid paralysis) and 'non-neuroinvasive disease' (West Nile fever); map neuroinvasive to cases_confirmed where lab-confirmed.

Confirmed cases require laboratory confirmation (IgM in CSF, PRNT, or PCR); probable cases typically have IgM in serum with epidemiologic linkage — ensure case classification is preserved in extraction.
CDPH weekly reports are cumulative year-to-date; to derive August-specific counts, subtract the July 31 cumulative total from the August 31 cumulative total where possible.
ArboNET data may lag real-time reporting by 1–2 weeks; August 2024 data may not be finalized until late September or October 2024.
Dead bird, sentinel chicken, and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — exclude from cases_confirmed/probable fields; they may be noted as contextual surveillance indicators only.
County-level reports may use 'suspected' or 'under investigation' categories that do not map directly to confirmed/probable — flag as cases_suspected or cases_unspecified accordingly.
Some county reports aggregate multi-week data; note the reporting period explicitly in evidence_quote to avoid double-counting across records.
disambiguation_risks: WNV surveillance reports often combine human and animal/vector data — isolate human case counts only.
'Cases' in some county reports may refer to mosquito pool positives or dead bird detections, not human infections — read context carefully.
Neuroinvasive disease case counts are a subset of total WNV human cases — do not add neuroinvasive + non-neuroinvasive if the source already reports a combined total.
CDPH reports are cumulative year-to-date; do not treat a single weekly report's total as the count for that week alone.
ArboNET data for 2024 may be preliminary and subject to revision — note data status (preliminary vs. final) in source metadata.
'Probable' case definitions vary between CDPH and CDC/ArboNET — document the case definition used by the source.
Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, and San Bernardino counties historically report the highest WNV burden in California — absence of data from these counties should trigger a data gap flag.
warnings: PIPELINE WARNING: task_input_warnings flag 'extraction_record_model_still_hantavirus_named' — verify that the extraction record schema and field mappings have been updated to West Nile virus before data entry; hantavirus-specific fields (e.g., pulmonary syndrome fields) must not be used.

PIPELINE WARNING: task_input_warnings flag 'source_discovery_not_yet_disease_generic' — source discovery logic may not yet be calibrated for arboviral/WNV-specific sources; manually verify that CDPH WNV surveillance pages and ArboNET are included in the source discovery scope.
DATA TIMING: August 2024 CDPH weekly WNV reports are the primary target; confirm that reports covering epidemiological weeks 31–35 (approximately August 1–31, 2024) are retrieved.
DATA COMPLETENESS: WNV case reporting has a known lag; August 2024 case counts may be incomplete in reports published before October 2024 — note data completeness status.
GEOGRAPHIC SCOPE: California has 58 counties; prioritize high-burden counties (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, San Bernardino, Riverside, Stanislaus) but do not exclude others.

West Nile virus (WNV) is a mosquito-borne virus that causes disease in humans, horses, and birds. WNV is common in the United States, especially in California, and is a problem that is here to stay. The best way to prevent WNV is to protect yourself from mosquito bites.

validation_source_categories: County-level health department press releases or situation reports
count_semantics_notes: CDPH and CDC ArboNET distinguish between 'neuroinvasive disease' (encephalitis, meningitis, acute flaccid paralysis) and 'non-neuroinvasive disease' (West Nile fever); map neuroinvasive to cases_confirmed where lab-confirmed.

Confirmed cases require laboratory confirmation (IgM in CSF, PRNT, or PCR); probable cases typically have IgM in serum with epidemiologic linkage — ensure case classification is preserved in extraction.
CDPH weekly reports are cumulative year-to-date; to derive August-specific counts, subtract the July 31 cumulative total from the August 31 cumulative total where possible.
ArboNET data may lag real-time reporting by 1–2 weeks; August 2024 data may not be finalized until late September or October 2024.
Dead bird, sentinel chicken, and mosquito pool positivity data are NOT human case counts — exclude from cases_confirmed/probable fields; they may be noted as contextual surveillance indicators only.
County-level reports may use 'suspected' or 'under investigation' categories that do not map directly to confirmed/probable — flag as cases_suspected or cases_unspecified accordingly.
Some county reports aggregate multi-week data; note the reporting period explicitly in evidence_quote to avoid double-counting across records.
disambiguation_risks: WNV surveillance reports often combine human and animal/vector data — isolate human case counts only.
'Cases' in some county reports may refer to mosquito pool positives or dead bird detections, not human infections — read context carefully.
Neuroinvasive disease case counts are a subset of total WNV human cases — do not add neuroinvasive + non-neuroinvasive if the source already reports a combined total.
CDPH reports are cumulative year-to-date; do not treat a single weekly report's total as the count for that week alone.
ArboNET data for 2024 may be preliminary and subject to revision — note data status (preliminary vs. final) in source metadata.
'Probable' case definitions vary between CDPH and CDC/ArboNET — document the case definition used by the source.
Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, and San Bernardino counties historically report the highest WNV burden in California — absence of data from these counties should trigger a data gap flag.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about West Nile Virus Disease.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
